data.title: Erémitisme et évangélisation: recherche sur l’influence de la vie d’Abraham de Quiduna dans les courants érémitiques de la Gaule du Nord
data.abstractNote: "La vie d'Abraham de Quiduna rédigée au VIe siècle, dans sa forme latine en même temps qu'elle l'était en grec et en syriaque fut découverte par Dom Wilmart en 1938 dans des feuillets en semi-onciales du VIIe siècle appartenant à l'abbaye de Corbie. Ce document fut diffusé dans la Gaule du Nord, dans des abbayes fondées ou en relation avec des ermites. Entre le manuscrit du VIIe siècle et les autres du XIe siècle l'écart est important, et la forme originelle céda la place à une forme révisée. Néanmoins les leçons de la vie d'Abraham furent reprises à travers les "vitae" des saints ermites. Deux thèmes ressortent: la fuite et l'évangélisation. Seule une démarche tendant vers l'humilité complète permet de redécouvrir l'Amour du prochain et favoriser un processus d'Evangélisation extérieure et de conversion interne. Les leçons de la "Vita Marinae Meretricis", nièce présumée d'Abraham ne font que compléter le discours initial. On observe cependant que cette partie du manuscrit fut surtout connue dans les monastères de moniales à partir du XIe siècle, époque à partir de laquelle l'Eglise renforça sa méfiance à l'égard des solitaires." data.title: St. Joseph’s University in Beirut and Its Institutions: Places of Knowledge of the Orient in the Christian East
data.abstractNote: This article examines the various institutions of the Université Saint-Joseph (U.S.J.) in Beirut, the works of its scholars, and their contributions to the knowledge of the Orient in the Christian East. The research question is the following: Were these prestigious institutions all "cultural symbols" of the knowledge of the Orient in the Christian East at the time? In order to answer the question, we particularly refer to the Oriental Library (La Bibliothèque Orientale); the creation of the Oriental Faculty; its publications, including the faculty's organ entitled Les Mélanges de la Faculté Orientale (Mélanges of the Eastern Faculty); the Catholic Printing Press, the journals Al-Machriq and Al-Bashir; and various other publications. Indeed, these institutions expanded the knowledge of the Orient to the students of the Université Saint-Joseph. This study is part of the scientific debate dealing with cultural, political history in the region.

data.title: The Revelationes of Pseudo-Methodius in the Eighth Century
data.abstractNote: This essay outlines the eighth-century distribution of copies of the Latin translation of the Revelationes of Pseudo-Methodius. If one takes into account a lost copy attested for the library of Bobbio, the pattern shows a distribution throughout the Columbanian foundations and associated Schottenklöster – Bobbio, St Gall, Reichenau, Tegernsee, Salzburg and Luxeuil (assuming that Bern, Burgerbibliothek 611, was written at that centre). Eighth-century copies also made their way to Tuscany and a centre in France. The earliest user of the Latin version was the author of The Cosmography of Aethicus Ister who pretended to be St Jerome. A case can be made that Ps. Jerome finished his book at Bobbio before the middle of the eighth century. The essay advances a textual argument that the lost Bobbio copy (Bo) is to be identified with Bern 611 (B) or else is related to it. The argument impugns the case that the existence of B, because it is the oldest dated copy (a. 727) and written in East Francia, proves that Petrus Monachus, the author of the Latin translation, had to have written it in that area. Given the lack of evidence for the study of Greek in eighth-century Merovingian Francia, it seems more plausible to assume that the translator worked in an Italian centre and received his Greek text from a Greek source to which his own house had a connection.

data.title: Apotropaic Autographs: Orality and Materiality in the Abgar-Jesus Inscriptions
data.abstractNote: In this paper, I explore the late antique tradition of inscribing the Abgar-Jesus correspondence on stone for protection as attested by seven inscriptions from Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, and Egypt. I first argue that the correspondence’s perceived protective efficacy stems from its claim to preserve an autograph of Jesus. I then explore the implications of embedding such an autograph into an urban landscape. Drawing on recent research on the orality and materiality of epigraphy, I suggest that the epigraphic attestations of the Abgar-Jesus correspondence join in a broader tradition of deploying oral formulae to protect domestic and civic space from harm, and therefore, should be viewed as ritually powerful objects that were “performing” the correspondence at their respective liminal spaces.

data.title: The Pilgrimage Center of St. Symeon the Younger: Designed by Angels, Supervised by a Saint, Constructed by Pilgrims
data.abstractNote: The present study evaluates the architectural characteristics of the building complex built around the column of St. Symeon the Younger at Wondrous Mountain/Antioch (Turkey) from different perspectives. The main focus remains on the architectural development of the site throughout the sixth century, although available archaeological and textual data concerning the preceding and successive periods is briefly presented. A full account of the state of the site at present is given in Chapter 2. This chapter is a detailed documentation of the remains and is strictly descriptive in nature. The historical sources are introduced and discussed in Chapter 3. The goal of this section is to elucidate the historical context under which the site was constructed and flourished. The focus is essentially the sixth century, while the later periods are presented cursorily. In Chapter 4, I discuss and reconstruct the development of the building complex. The section aims at establishing a clearer picture of each building phase. This process also involves contextualizing the architectural features and design decisions within each period whenever possible, while reconsidering the historical discussions presented in the previous chapter. Chapter 5 discusses how the site should be reconsidered in light of other examples of the Early Byzantine period. To do this, I compare the site of St. Symeon the Younger with other stylite sites, especially the Syrian ones, as well as with other pilgrimage centers of the period. Finally, I propose that the complex at Wondrous Mountain was originally an unconventional pilgrimage site in the sixth century, because of the need to establish a site appropriate for a living and immobile saint who is active in liturgical practices. Towards the end of the saint’s life, the site was prepared for the aftermath of his death and it was transformed into a site including a new veneration route to its south.

data.abstractNote: Le présent papier s’attache à mettre en lumière quelques aspects parfois méconnus dans les relations et dans les perceptions intercommunautaires chrétiennes, et ce au sein du comté de Tripoli où prévalait de fait un contexte religieux multiconfessionnel doublé d’un substrat de melting-pot socio-culturel. data.title: Le baptême du Christ sur l’icône bilatérale de Kaftoun et son rapport avec la Vierge Hodigitria
data.abstractNote: The Kaftoun icon (mid-third quarter of the thirteenth century) is a two-sided panel with the figure of the Virgin Hodigitria (Conductor) on one side and Jesus’ baptism on the other. The Baptism scene emphasizes the divine nature of Jesus, announced and prefigured by the prophets of the Old Testament depicted scene in the upper corners of the panel. The icon with its two sides, the Virgin Hodegitria emphasizing the human nature of Jesus, and the baptism his divine nature, says the hypostatic union of the two natures of Jesus. Some ancient texts associate the rite of baptism with rivers and other water sources, where sanctification could take place. This is why the link of the Kaftoun icon with the ritual of baptism on the day of the Epiphany is plausible, especially as the monastery is located at the edge of Nahr el-Jaouz river. The panel was held so that the image of the Virgin, to whom was dedicated the monastery, was directed forward while the baptism scene was facing the congregation. All this testifies to the liturgical function of the icon.

data.title: Aid to the Syrians (1916–17): A Failure
data.abstractNote: In 1915, the Ottoman province of Syria, especially the Lebanese mountain area inhabited by the Maronite Christians, was isolated, on the one hand, by the armies of Djemal Pasha and on the other, by the naval and economic blockade established by the British and the French. Locusts also ruined the crops in the same year and famine ensued; this famine would lead to the death of about 500,000 Syrian people. Relief organizations tried to take supplies to Syria. They had to organize transport of supplies and to obtain permission to distribute them. They appealed to the representatives of the neutral nations in vain. From 1916, there were many who hoped that Pope Benedict XV would intercede. The latter lent an ear to them for humanitarian reasons, to protect the Holy Places and to be in a position to negotiate the status of the Vatican after the war. He encouraged apostolic nuncios and delegates to find the way to take the humanitarian aid to the Syrian population through contact with the Ottoman authorities and by means of Spanish representatives. However, the Ottomans refusal to recognize the emergency situation, the strategic and military imperatives of the belligerents and the underlying wish of the papal diplomacy to be recognized after the war caused every attempt to fail.
